content.text: The Full List With Context

To sell digital products from Africa to international buyers, follow these 5 steps: deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack using cloud infrastructure, set up automatic on-chain crypto payments with NOWPayments, store order data in a decentralized database like Supabase, deliver files through a cloud storage solution like Cloudflare R2, and configure your domain for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to prevent email spoofing. This setup empowers creators to reach a global audience, no matter their location or the currencies they use. By leveraging NOWPayments' 300+ cryptocurrency support and competitive fees, especially on recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON, creators can minimize transaction costs and maximize revenue. This comprehensive approach to digital commerce not only resolves payment issues but also ensures infrastructure sovereignty for creators, giving them full control over their online stores and customer data. By choosing this route, creators can build a future-proof digital commerce business that is not reliant on Stripe or any other payment platform.
Why Each Item on This List Matters

Deploying a sovereign digital commerce stack is crucial because it allows creators to own and operate their own infrastructure, free from the restrictions and fees of third-party payment platforms. By setting up automatic on-chain crypto payments, creators can accept payments in multiple cryptocurrencies, reducing the risk of payment failures and providing a seamless experience for their customers. Storing order data in a decentralized database ensures data ownership and control, while delivering files through a cloud storage solution like Cloudflare R2 ensures fast and secure file transfer. Configuring your domain for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC prevents email spoofing and maintains a professional image. These steps are the building blocks of a robust digital commerce stack that can handle the demands of a global audience.
The Ones Most Creators Get Wrong

Many creators in Africa make the mistake of relying on workarounds like PayPal and Stripe, which come with high fees and restrictive policies. Others try to use local payment gateways, which may not support international transactions. Furthermore, some creators overlook the importance of infrastructure sovereignty, leading to a lack of control over their online stores and customer data. By following the 5 steps outlined above, creators can avoid these common pitfalls and build a strong, scalable digital commerce business that is not limited by payment restrictions or infrastructure limitations.

It's also essential to consider the cost-benefit analysis of implementing a sovereign digital commerce stack, taking into account the fees associated with NOWPayments and the long-term benefits of infrastructure sovereignty. By weighing the pros and cons, creators can make informed decisions and prioritize their implementation roadmap accordingly.
